title: Discovery: Aperture Dynamics - Private/VPC deployment
topics: Region constraints and data residency (eu-west-1 requirement)
Network architecture: CIDR overlap, route tables, NAT, Transit Gateway
Authentication & encryption: KMS/HSM, SAML/SSO, audit logs
Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs: latency, cost, data egress
summary: Initial discovery for Private/VPC deployment. Customer requires private connectivity from their AWS VPC to Redwood private deployment in eu-west-1, strong compliance controls (audit logs, KMS integration), and clarification on peering options (VPC peering, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink). Discussed network requirements (CIDR, route tables, NAT), region constraints, and next steps: share peering diagram, security docs, and provide pricing estimate for Dedicated + Private deployment.
next_steps: Samir to share Redwood private endpoints / PrivateLink design + VPC peering doc
Leah to produce initial latency/cost estimate for eu-west-1 dedicated pool
Schedule security deep dive with Aperture InfoSec next Thursday
Customer to share current VPC CIDR ranges and proxy/NAT architecture
action_items: Samir Patel | Send draft SOW + pricing | 2026-01-20
Leah Chen | Run 8k-context latency/cost estimate and recommend instance types | 2026-01-18

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Chen (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Aperture CTO), Liam O'Connor (Aperture SRE), Priya Nair (Aperture Security), Jonas Keller (Platform)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh, super excited to chat through your Private deployment needs. quick rundowns - I'm Samir, I'm the account lead, Leah's our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Marta: Thanks, Samir. I'll kick off with a little context. Aperture Dynamics is building a recommendation microservice that runs sensitive customer signals, so we need the inference stack inside our VPC, no egress to internet for model inputs.
[00:26] Leah: Got it. So you're looking at Redwood Private, VPC-based deployment, right? Any constraints on region or residency?
[00:31] Marta: Yes, must be in eu-west-1 for data residency and local latency.
[00:36] Leah: Okay, eu-west-1 is supported for Private deployments. We have a few connectivity options - VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or PrivateLink / AWS PrivateLink-style private endpoints. Each has tradeoffs.
[00:47] Liam: Quick question on scale - we'll have spikes up to ~600 qps during US hours, most traffic originates from eu-west and also some cross-region from us-west via our app tier. We need predictability and burst handling.
[00:58] Samir: For spikes we usually recommend Dedicated capacity with autoscale and burst pools; for Private you can pin a Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 and route traffic privately. We'll cover routing options in a sec.
[01:10] Priya: From security perspective we need: KMS integration for keys, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, SAML SSO, RBAC, and no plaintext logs leaving our VPC. Also need to ensure CIDR non-overlap and no transitive peering surprises.
[01:25] Leah: Yeah, all reasonable. On KMS - Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (KMS) for encrypting data at rest in our private deployment; we can integrate with your KMS via cross-account grants. Audit logs can be shipped to an S3 bucket in your account or forwarded to your SIEM over private connections.
[01:41] Jonas: What about networking specifics - do you require us to create peering, or does Redwood provision an ENI/endpoint into our VPC?
[01:49] Samir: Good question. We have multiple patterns. One is classic VPC peering where we peer the Redwood VPC to your VPC and you route specific prefixes. Another is a PrivateLink endpoint where you create an Interface Endpoint in your VPC that talks to an endpoint service on our side - that avoids route table complexity and works well if you have Transit Gateway or overlap concerns. Transit Gateway is also an option for customers who already use it for central networking.
[02:12] Liam: We do use a Transit Gateway regionally but not cross-account attachments yet. If we peer with you, we need to confirm non-transitive nature - we can't route from our internal VPC to some other VPC through your peering.
[02:25] Leah: Exactly; VPC peering is non-transitive. If you need central hub-and-spoke, Transit Gateway is the recommended approach. PrivateLink is simpler for non-overlapping CIDRs and when you want to avoid touching route tables much.
[02:37] Marta: Is there a bandwidth limit or throughput consideration on PrivateLink vs peering? We have large models and, uh, sometimes push big context payloads.
[02:45] Samir: PrivateLink is typically fine for control-plane and inference traffic - it can handle high throughput but there are interface endpoint ENI limits and per-ENI bandwidth characteristics. For very high sustained throughput, peering or Transit Gateway with direct pathing can be more predictable. We'll capture expected TPS and payload sizes in the SOW.
[02:58] Priya: About IP addressing - our infra team said our VPC uses 10.10.0.0/16, we also have shared services in 10.11.0.0/16. Do you require our end to change CIDRs?
[03:06] Leah: We don't require changing them, but they must not overlap with the Redwood private VPC ranges. If there is overlap we can use PrivateLink. If neither is possible we can discuss NATed architectures but that's more complex.
[03:18] Jonas: What about DNS resolution? We want to resolve private hostnames to Redwood endpoints internally.
[03:23] Samir: With PrivateLink you can set up private DNS so that your service hostnames resolve to the interface endpoint IPs. With peering, you point the route for the prefix to the peered VPC and use internal DNS forwarding if needed. We'll share a doc with recommended DNS setups.
[03:36] Liam: Are there TLS/mTLS options? We prefer mutual TLS between our app tier and the inference endpoints.
[03:41] Leah: We support TLS by default. mTLS is supported for customer-to-Redwood communications in Private deployments; we'll need to coordinate cert exchange and the SAML/Security setup. There can be terminations at the private endpoint depending on the architecture - we typically terminate TLS at the instance but we can front with a layer that handles mTLS.
[03:55] Marta: Also curious about logging - can we ensure that model outputs are not retained outside the VPC?
[04:00] Samir: Yes, for Private deployments we can configure no persistence of request payloads in our control plane and ensure logs are stored only in your account/S3. We'll include the exact retention controls in the security pack.
[04:11] Priya: SOC2 / ISO attestation? We need to review evidence for vendors handling inference workloads.
[04:16] Leah: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and can provide our compliance pack. For Private deployments we provide additional documentation on how the control plane interacts and what data leaves the tenant boundary. We'll share the compliance artifacts under NDA.
[04:28] Liam: Network flow - do you require NAT gateways or do you allow zero egress? We want zero egress to internet from the inference instances.
[04:35] Samir: You can absolutely have zero internet egress. In that model your VPC will have route tables pointing only to private endpoints or peered routes; the instances will not require NAT. For certain operations (image pulls, OS updates) we recommend an update window where a temporary egress can be allowed via endpoints, or you can use an internal repo/mirror.
[04:51] Marta: Let's talk about cross-region calls - we have some US traffic. If the inference is in eu-west-1, what's the latency profile for US -> EU?
[04:58] Leah: You're looking at cross-continent RTTs; for single-token generation maybe ~120-200ms extra on top of model generation. For low-latency needs in US, you could deploy a dedicated pool in us-west and route low-latency requests there, and have the eu-west pool for residency-sensitive data. We can also do model routing by policy, so non-sensitive requests go to hosted or us-west.
[05:19] Liam: Do you support routing based on metadata? Like route if request.flag_sensitive == true -> eu-west private pool?
[05:25] Samir: Yep that's part of the smart routing - you can configure rules to route by header, tag, or tenant to different pools or fallbacks. We'll show examples.
[05:33] Jonas: Any constraints on subnets - do you need public subnets for load balancers or can everything be private subnets?
[05:39] Leah: Everything can be in private subnets. Our private deployment uses internal load balancers and private ENIs, so public subnets are not required. If you want internet egress for updates you can use NAT or VPC endpoints.
[05:50] Marta: Okay, what's the typical timeline to get a Private deployment up in eu-west-1 with Dedicated pool? We're targeting mid-Feb for pilot.
[05:57] Samir: For a pilot it's usually 3-6 weeks: network design + peering setup (1 week), provisioning dedicated pool and model onboarding (1-2 weeks), validation and security review (1-2 weeks). We can tighten if both sides prioritize.
[06:10] Priya: For onboarding you'll need access to our staging environment for benchmarking. Do you need keys or can you run black-box tests?
[06:16] Leah: Black-box tests are possible for latency and throughput, but for deeper profiling (KV cache, batch tuning) it's better to get test traffic in a controlled staging VPC. We can provide a benchmarking harness that you can run inside your VPC to exercise endpoints.
[06:29] Liam: On model sizes - are there quantization options? We run a 13B tuned model, want to understand latency/cost tradeoffs.
[06:35] Leah: We support quantized runtimes; our runtime picks kernel implementations by model architecture and quantization. For 13B, quantized 4-bit can reduce memory and cost with some perf tradeoffs; we'll run benchmarks against your workload as part of the poc.
[06:48] Marta: What about backup connectivity - if the private link goes down do you provide failover to Redwood hosted endpoints?
[06:54] Samir: We can configure fallback to a hosted endpoint or another region/pool. That's part of the rollout policy - canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to reduce downtime. We'll propose an RTO/RPO in the SOW.
[07:07] Priya: We have a legal requirement to keep audit trails for 7 years. Can you forward all audit events to our SIEM?
[07:13] Leah: Yes, we can push audit logs to your S3 bucket + CloudTrail-like events, and forward to your SIEM; we'll align the schema and retention policy.
[07:23] Jonas: Are there any AWS service limits we should be aware of - e.g., ENI limits in the account for PrivateLink?
[07:30] Samir: Yes, interface endpoints create ENIs per AZ, so there are soft limits. If you have very large scale with many endpoints we recommend discussing limits with AWS in advance or using peering/Transit Gateway for predictable scale.
[07:43] Liam: For perf benchmarks - what metrics will you provide? p95 latency, p99, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens?
[07:49] Leah: We'll provide latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), throughput, GPU utilization, tokens per second, and cost breakdown per token. We'll also include KV cache hit rates and recommendations for batching settings.
[08:00] Marta: Any special IAM roles required for integration?
[08:03] Leah: We'll ask you to create an IAM role for S3 access for logs, and possibly a cross-account role for KMS grants. We'll provide templates in the network/security doc.
[08:12] Samir: Alright, quick demo of the network diagrams - (Samir shares screen) here's the PrivateLink pattern and here's the peering + Transit Gateway pattern.
[08:24] [screen share noises / typing]
[08:28] Leah: Note the non-transitive note on the peering illustration - you can't route through our VPC to another. Also the PrivateLink shows Private DNS option to resolve api.redwood.private -> 10.2.3.4 in your VPC.
[08:40] Jonas: That Private DNS looks cleaner for our infra team, fewer route table changes.
[08:44] Liam: But I'm thinking about throughput - is there a hard cap on concurrent connections?
[08:49] Leah: No hard cap from Redwood side; AWS enforces some soft limits. We typically size the dedicated pool to handle your concurrency and use autoscaling policies.
[08:58] Marta: On cost: what's the delta between Hosted API vs Dedicated private pool? ballpark.
[09:04] Samir: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated private pool has a capacity commit and then per-token costs tied to that pool. For high steady throughput Dedicated tends to be more economical. We'll provide a modeled comparison in the pricing sheet.
[09:15] Priya: For SAML/SSO we need SCIM for provisioning accounts. Do you support SCIM?
[09:20] Leah: Yes, SCIM is supported for user provisioning. We'll include SAML/SCIM setup docs.
[09:26] Marta: Anything else we should be aware of for the pilot?
[09:29] Samir: We'll need your CIDRs, the VPC admin contact, preferred connectivity option (PrivateLink vs peering), and a list of models you intend to test. Once we have that we'll produce the SOW and a provisioning timeline.
[09:40] Priya: I'll take the VPC CIDR, we use 10.10.0.0/16 and shared 10.11.0.0/16; Jonas will confirm Transit Gateway availability.
[09:47] Jonas: Also to note, our current egress policies block outbound internet from the compute subnets; we'll need a plan for image updates or we can mirror images internally.
[09:55] Leah: We can support that - using private mirrors or scheduled maintenance windows.
[10:00] Marta: Great. A few nitty-gritty questions: do you support Bring-Your-Own-HSM?
[10:05] Leah: We support customer-managed KMS; BYO-HSM is more involved but possible through partners. We'll flag that for the security session.
[10:13] Liam: For performance testing, can we run a bench harness against your staging private endpoint before we sign?
[10:18] Samir: Yes, we can provision a short-lived staging endpoint or run the benchmark inside your VPC. We'll coordinate credentials and the harness - Leah will follow up.
[10:27] Priya: On legal - data deletion proofs? We need to show deletion of logs and data upon contract end.
[10:32] Samir: We'll include data deletion procedures in the SOW and the compliance pack, including support for data export and deletion proofs via logs.
[10:40] Marta: Any red flags or common gotchas you see with customers doing this?
[10:44] Leah: Overlapping CIDRs is a common blocker; also not planning for ENI/service quota increases in AWS. Another is assuming peering is transitive - that trips up routing. Lastly, not validating certificate rotation/mTLS. We'll provide a pre-provisioning checklist.
[10:58] Jonas: Let's talk about maintenance windows - we require notifications for restarts that might affect latency.
[11:03] Samir: For Dedicated Private we can agree on maintenance windows; emergency patches are communicated via the console and email, and we can gate restarts to off-peak windows.
[11:17] Marta: I think that's a good stopping point. Can we recap next steps?
[11:22] Samir: Sure. Recap: 1) Samir to share PrivateLink + peering network doc and sample Terraform snippets; 2) Leah will run a latency/cost estimate and recommend instance types for your 13B model; 3) Schedule security deep dive with Priya next Thursday; 4) Aperture to send CIDR ranges and confirm Transit Gateway availability.
[11:40] Priya: We'll aim to have CIDRs and TGW confirmation by Monday.
[11:44] Samir: Great. I'll send a calendar invite for the security deep dive and a pricing sheet. Thanks everyone.
[11:50] Marta: Thanks, Samir. Appreciate it.
[11:53] Leah: Thanks all.
[11:55] End of recording.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hears and truncated words; refer to follow-up docs for exact Terraform snippets and compliance artifacts.
